Marianne Brandt, tea infuser MT 49

A small metal teapot composed of a hemisphere, a disc, a cylinder, and a half-circle handle on a cross-shaped foot.

Source
Bauhaus Kooperation: Tee-Extraktkännchen (MT 49)
Creator
Marianne Brandt
Made
1924
Style
Bauhaus (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Precise, geometric, refined
Evidence
Downloaded and inspected Lucia Moholy’s 1924 photograph of the infuser on the Bauhaus Kooperation page, in the scratchpad only. The Met record gives materials and dimensions.
Reviewed
25 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Bauhaus Kooperation says Brandt made the infuser in her first year of study, 1924, in the metal workshop under László Moholy-Nagy, and that the Bauhaus often criticized the use of costly materials such as silver and ebony. Bauhaus Kooperation.

The Met holds an example: “Tea Infuser and Strainer,” ca. 1924, silver and ebony, 8.3 × 10.8 × 16.5 cm, accession 2000.63a–c. The Met 491299.

Observed

  • The body is a polished metal hemisphere that reflects its surroundings.
  • A flat disc lid sits on a short cylinder; a small black cylindrical knob sits on top.
  • The handle is a flat black half-disc, fixed to the body with a rectangular bracket.
  • A short straight spout projects at left.
  • The body rests on a small crossed foot.

Why it belongs

The infuser shows the Bauhaus approach to form in three dimensions: each part is one elementary solid, and the parts meet without transitions. It is the object equivalent of circles and bars in a poster.

Borrow

Build a component from separate elementary shapes and keep the joins visible.

Contrast one polished or bright material with one flat black part.
